transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-07 11:00 PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: zoom_us_link_placeholder
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Banerjee (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood), Maya Chen (AstralHealth), Omar Reyes (AstralHealth), Sana Patel (AstralHealth), Noah Li (AstralHealth)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):

- Benchmarks and success criteria agreed at a high level: p95 latency target, throughput, quality checks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Jordan from Redwood here, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:14] Maya Chen: Maya here, Head of Platform. Omar, Sana and Noor-- Noah are on.
[00:19] Omar Reyes: Yep, Omar in security.
[00:23] Priya Banerjee: Priya, SE focusing on networking and perf.
[00:27] Sana Patel: Sana, ML eng, I'll be running the prompts.
[00:31] Liam O'Connor: Liam, solutions eng, will help with bench infra.
[00:35] Jordan Miles: Awesome. Goal of the call: scope a POC for private deployment — specifically private networking (VPC peering or PrivateLink), egress constraints, and EU data residency requirements. We'll sketch success criteria, sizing, and a timeline.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Quick background: we run clinical search + summarization, all PHI-adjacent data. Regs require EU-only residency for a subset of traffic and no public internet egress. We're evaluating Redwood's private offering and need to validate network isolation and auditability.

[01:40] Priya Banerjee: Understood. From an architectural view Redwood Private can be deployed in a VPC in your AWS account and we support either classic VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. For GCP we have Private Service Connect options — sometimes the speech-to-text got that as Private ServiceConnect, sorry — but they are equivalent for private connectivity.

[02:10] Noah Li: We prefer peering because it avoids extra hop costs but security team likes PrivateLink since it limits the surface. Also we have strict egress rules: only allowed outbound to our data lake S3 endpoints and our SIEM. No NAT gateway to internet. Is that compatible?

[02:45] Priya Banerjee: Yes, peering works fine if you restrict route tables and security groups. PrivateLink can be locked down to specific ENIs and doesn’t require route propagation, so security folks prefer that pattern. We can support both; depends on your VPC design and compliance.

[03:12] Omar Reyes: Two things: 1) We need KMS integration — keys must be in our customer-managed KMS (CMK) and ideally HSM-backed. 2) Audit logs must be forwarded to our Splunk cluster and retained for 7 years.

[03:40] Jordan Miles: We support KMS integrations — Redwood Private can be configured to use your CMK for model artifacts and logs encryption. HSM-backed keys are supported via your cloud provider. Audit logging and forwarding to external endpoints is in the roadmap and we have existing customers streaming to Splunk; we'll include specifics in the security pack.

[04:05] Sana Patel: For the POC we'll run two workloads: a clinical Q&A model (2k token context) and a summarization pipeline (~800 tokens). We want to test latency p95 under 20 concurrent requests and sustained throughput at 100 req/s. Also cost per 1M tokens is an evaluation metric.

[04:38] Priya Banerjee: Good. Proposed bench plan: 1) Cold start latencies (KV cache cold) with 1, 5, 20 concurrent; 2) Warm cache throughput at 100 req/s for 10 minutes; 3) p95 and p99 measurements, and token accounting for cost modeling. We'll use a 1k prompt sample set that Sana will provide.

[05:10] Sana Patel: We'll prepare 1k prompts and label expected behaviors for quality checks. Also note: some prompts have PHI redaction requirements, can Redwood run redaction pre-processing?

[05:30] Jordan Miles: We have built-in redaction examples in the SDK and can run a preprocess in your VPC layer, or you can send pre-redacted inputs. We'll include options in the bench plan.

[06:00] Maya Chen: Regarding region residency: for any EU-only traffic we need compute and logs to stay in eu-west-1. For US traffic we can use us-east-1. Cross-region replication is disallowed for the EU subset. Is that possible with Redwood?

[06:28] Priya Banerjee: Yes, you can pin model endpoints to a specific region. Redwood Private can be provisioned in multiple regions. Policies can route EU keys to eu-west-1 and we will not replicate logs outside that region if configured. We'll want to validate this in the POC run.

[06:55] Omar Reyes: Encryption in transit — mTLS endpoint? We need mutual TLS and certs managed by us or via ACM.

[07:10] Priya Banerjee: We support mTLS for internal endpoints and can integrate with ACM or customer certs. We'll add the cert management options in the security pack.

[07:30] Liam O'Connor: For the bench network setup, we'll need a maintenance window to provision peering / endpoints. Also, if you choose PrivateLink, you'll have to create interface endpoints and we'll provide the service name. If peering, we provide the peering CIDR ranges.

[07:58] Noah Li: How about IP space — do you require overlapping or non-overlapping CIDRs? We have limited available /16s due to our corporate malarkey—stuff in other accounts.

[08:12] Priya Banerjee: We require non-overlapping ranges for VPC peering. For PrivateLink you don't need unique CIDR because it's an ENI-based flow, less likely to collide. We'll send you the recommended CIDR ranges and an architecture diagram.

[08:45] Maya Chen: Success criteria — what do you suggest we use to mark POC success?

[08:55] Jordan Miles: From Redwood's side, suggested success metrics: 1) Connectivity and data residency validated (no exfiltration paths), 2) Performance: p95 latency < 150ms for the sub-800 token workload, p95 < 300ms for 2k token Q&A (these are rough targets—can calibrate), 3) Throughput: sustain 100 req/s warm cache without error rates >1%, 4) Security: KMS + mTLS validated, audit logs forwarding configured, 5) Quality: model responses meet your annotated acceptance rate >= 92% on the sample set.

[09:40] Sana Patel: Those latency targets sound aggressive for 2k context, curious what model flavor we'll run — are you suggesting an Llama2-like model or a smaller candidate?

[09:56] Priya Banerjee: We can run multiple model variants during the POC. Typically we test the curated open models in our catalog — smaller models give better latency/cost tradeoffs. We can also run a quantized variant on the same hardware to explore cost reductions. We'll include a matrix: model x sequence length x quantization profile.

[10:25] Omar Reyes: For the benchmarking, we need attestation that logs and telemetry do not include full prompt text (PII). Can you redact logs?

[10:40] Jordan Miles: Logs can be configured to redact inputs; by default only metadata is emitted but we can apply redaction rules. We'll provide the log schema and redaction knobs.

[11:05] Maya Chen: Timeline — we want a two-week technical POC, followed by a decision meeting. Is that feasible?

[11:18] Priya Banerjee: Typical POC timeline we propose: Week 0: network setup and access (1 week ideally to handle approvals), Week 1: bench runs and smoke tests, Week 2: analysis and joint review. So total ~3 calendar weeks from kickoff to final review if network approvals are faster. Two weeks is tight but possible if we get CIDRs and whitelists same day and there are no procurement delays.

[11:48] Noah Li: Our procurement window is usually 10 business days. Can we run discovery in parallel while procurement runs?

[11:55] Jordan Miles: Yes — we can do the technical POC with a temporary contract or MSA addendum and move procurement in parallel. We'll flag legal for a streamlined pilot agreement.

[12:12] Sana Patel: For load generation, do you recommend we use our k6 scripts or do you have a harness?

[12:18] Liam O'Connor: We typically run a mixed harness: our internal bench runner plus reference k6 scripts so results are comparable to other customers. We'll share the harness repo.

[12:30] Maya Chen: Ok, about data residency: if a request originates from EU but uses a model in US for cost reasons, is that acceptable if payload is not stored and ephemeral? Our legal says compute must remain in EU for EU-tagged requests.

[12:48] Priya Banerjee: We can route EU-tagged requests to EU pinned endpoints; cross-region model fallback is possible but would violate your residency constraint. So we will honor region pinning in the POC. We can also show an audit trail that no cross-region calls occurred.

[13:10] Omar Reyes: Any managed NAT or egress through Redwood-managed endpoints? We strictly disallow internet egress.

[13:20] Priya Banerjee: For Private deployments in your VPC there is no forced egress through Redwood-managed NAT. All egress is in your control; we only ask for specific outbound connectivity to our management endpoints if you opt for a control plane connection. There is also an option for an out-of-band air-gapped config, more complex but possible.

[13:48] Jordan Miles: We'll likely recommend the control-plane traffic be minimized and tunneled over a private connection or via API over a dedicated peering. We'll propose both options in the documentation.

[14:05] Sana Patel: Bench specifics — will you measure cold-start with KV cache misses? We saw a prior doc where Kv cache was pronounced K-V cash in the transcript, just noting transcription humor.

[14:22] Priya Banerjee: Ha, yes K-V cache. We'll measure cold start (cache cold) and warm ongoing. We'll also measure token-per-second and op/s. We'll include payload sizes and payload tokenization breakdown so cost modeling is precise.

[14:45] Maya Chen: Ok so concrete asks from us now: CIDR ranges, which subnets can host endpoints, and where Splunk / KMS endpoints sit.

[14:58] Noah Li: We'll extract CIDR ranges and a support window. Expect a ticket by end of day tomorrow.

[15:05] Jordan Miles: Great. Priya, can you run through the bench plan items and deliverables?

[15:12] Priya Banerjee: Sure. Deliverables: 1) Network checklist (peering vs private link steps), 2) Security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, cert options, log schema), 3) Benchmark plan (1k prompts, test harness, metrics to capture), 4) Quote incl. estimated token costs and dedicated capacity options. We'll also attach a sample runbook for the bench.

[15:40] Omar Reyes: One more thing: are there any baseline SLA or latency guarantees for Dedicated capacity? We may need 99.9 latency SLA for certain calls.

[15:52] Jordan Miles: Dedicated (Reserved) capacity is an option — that comes with SLA commitments and predictable throughput. We'll include the SLA options and pricing tiers in the quote.

[16:05] Sana Patel: For quality thresholds — we will use a 1k annotated set, require >=92% acceptance for the clinical Q&A. If below that we may ask to try different model or tuning.

[16:20] Priya Banerjee: Sounds good. We'll include guidance on model selection and quantization impacts. Note: some highly quantized models show regressions on edge-case medical prompts, so we'll flag trade-offs.

[16:40] Maya Chen: Any red flags we should watch?

[16:45] Liam O'Connor: Potential snag is procurement/legal timing and firewall approvals for peering. Also if your account CIDR is tightly allocated it may push PrivateLink as the only path, which has slightly higher ops overhead.

[17:05] Omar Reyes: Also need to validate that we can enforce no logs containing full prompt texts in any telemetry forwarded to Redwood-managed control plane.

[17:20] Jordan Miles: We'll provide a telemetry schema and redaction config.

[17:30] Priya Banerjee: We'll also do a quick smoke test with a synthetic prompt during the setup phase to confirm regional routing and KMS encryption.

[17:48] Maya Chen: Sounds like a plan. Can you put dates on the sequence?

[17:54] Jordan Miles: Proposed timeline: 2025-04-09 deliver security pack/network diagram; 2025-04-10 Astral provides CIDRs/whitelist window; week of 2025-04-21 run bench; 2025-04-28 review results and decision. We'll confirm calendar invites after the call.

[18:18] Noah Li: We'll try to expedite firewall approvals. Procurement will start parallel.

[18:30] Sana Patel: One last Q on metrics: will you provide raw bench data and scripts?

[18:37] Liam O'Connor: Yes, raw CSVs, dashboards, and the harness will be shared in a repo link.

[18:50] Jordan Miles: Cool. Any other questions from Astral?
[18:55] Maya Chen: Not right now. Omar, anything on security?

[19:00] Omar Reyes: No, covered. We'll look for the security pack.

[19:05] Jordan Miles: Ok recap: Redwood to send network checklist, security pack (SOC2/ISO/docs), bench plan and quote by 2025-04-09. Astral to send CIDR ranges and firewall window by 2025-04-10. Schedule bench wk of 2025-04-21. Follow up review on 2025-04-28.

[19:25] Maya Chen: Thank you, speak soon.
[19:30] Jordan Miles: Thanks everyone. End of call.
